name: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
problem: Evaluating LLM chat assistants on open-ended questions is expensive and existing benchmarks don't measure human preferences well.
mechanism: Uses strong LLMs (GPT-4) as judges to evaluate model outputs on MT-Bench (multi-turn questions) and Chatbot Arena (crowdsourced battles). Documents position bias, verbosity bias, and self-enhancement bias. Achieves >80% agreement with human preferences.
notes:
Published at NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (verified from arXiv comments). This paper is foundational for LLM evaluation methodology but also illustrates the contamination problem: the same LLM-as-a-judge paradigm is now widely used, and the benchmarks themselves (MT-Bench, Chatbot Arena) are now potentially contaminated by training data. The paper documents biases (position, verbosity, self-enhancement) that must be controlled for.
